sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: How does one very large value affect mean and median?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 24 yes, 10 no; row 2: 6 yes, 16 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 15x + 36, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional test points is associated with 15 more hour studieds.
The predicted value is 15 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 15 test points.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 15 test points.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set records 9, 15, 13, 19, 19. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 15, median 15
mean 15, median 13
mean 16, median 15
mean 15, median 16

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 227 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 7 yes, 14 no; row 2: 41 yes, 42 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 10x + 16, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 10 test points.
The predicted value is 10 test points when x is 0.
Each additional test points is associated with 10 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 10 test points.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales and swimming-pool admissions are strongly positively correlated across a year. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
